newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil ends firm on nervous European market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil ends firm on nervous European market.

text.p: Palm oil prices finished higher on Tuesday on a nervous European vegetable oil market as a squeeze built up in nearby positions.
Traders said problems in loading a vessel in Malaysia were the cause of a tightness in nearby supplies of crude palm oil which set up a squeeze.
"It's only one vessel that is involved but it creates a gap and shipments have to be pushed back to make way for the oil that cannot be move in that vessel," said a trader.
"People are getting nervous over the delay and prices will keep going up until the bubble bursts and then we'll be back to where we started," said another traded.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $7.50 to $12.50 up after Dec traded from $562.50 up to $575, Mar at $550 and Jan at $557.50 and $560.00.
Refined palm oil prices closed $5.00 to $10 higher underpinned by gains in the Far East on talk of fresh tenders from Pakistan.
News that India is to import 50,000 tonnes of sunflower seed oil from the United States for Dec-Jan shipment had no impact.
Gains in palm oil had supported lauric oils prices earlier in the day but by the close coconut oil was unchanged to $10 down and palmkernel oil unchanged to $5.00 up.
Afloat coconut oil traded at $830, Nov/Dec at $825, Dec/Jan at from $785 up to $790 and back down to $780. Jan/Feb traded from $565 up to $567.50 and then back to $560 a tonne cif.
Soft oils were little changed from the opening in a tradeless market.
Soyoil closed 0.50 guilders up to 0.25 guilders down and rape oil 0.25 to 1.25 guilders lower.
Based on sellers' prices, the premium for rape oil over soyoil was 2.50 to 4.25 guilders at the close against one to 4.50 on Monday.
